terra.problem: The passage does not say whether Pashhur asked for prayer or what he was looking for.
The passage does not establish that Pashhur skipped a meeting or that there were no questions or explanations.
Saying Jeremiah did not come out whispering or quiet adds a volume and manner of speaking the text does not give.
The passage does not record Jeremiah thanking Pashhur, but it does not establish that he thanked him for nothing.
The text says Pashhur released Jeremiah the next day; it does not say Jeremiah spent a night in the stocks.
The explanation says terror is something that comes upon a person, while the LORD says Pashhur will be a terror to himself and his friends.
The passage does not say where Jeremiah and Pashhur live.
Calling the threatened captivity a road trip makes light of the suffering in the passage.
The claim that Assyria appears elsewhere in the Bible needs a reference.
The passage does not say that nobody buries anything under the temple; it says the wealth will be carried away.
The prophecy says Pashhur will go to Babylon and die and be buried there. It does not say he will stay there without leaving.
The prophecy does not rule out an escape or a trip home before Pashhur dies and is buried in Babylon.
Saying he will not joke about the line comments on how he tells the passage.
Pashhur is the one who prophesied the lies; his friends are the ones he prophesied them to. The explanation incorrectly includes Pashhur among the recipients.
